column8: CDC Field Epidemiology Manual · https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/analyze-interpret-data.html · risk, rates and interpreting comparisons

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A registry observes 12 first events over 600 person-years at risk with staggered entry. What is the incidence rate per 1,000 person-years?
column7: 12/600 × 1,000 = 20. Person-time accounts for differing observation lengths.
column8: CDC, Principles of Epidemiology · https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/csels/dsepd/ss1978/lesson3/ · measures of frequency, association and public health impact

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A trial reports p = 0.04 in women and p = 0.11 in men. Without an interaction estimate, is this evidence that the treatment effect differs by sex?
column6: No. Compare the treatment effects directly with their uncertainty.
column7: A difference in subgroup significance can reflect sample size even when effects are identical.
column8: ICH E9 · https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/E9_Guideline.pdf · sections 3 and 5, trial size, estimation, multiplicity and subgroups

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A paper labels its analysis intention-to-treat but many outcomes are unknown in one arm. Does the label resolve potential bias?
column6: No. Examine missingness, assumptions and sensitivity analyses.
column7: Keeping original group labels does not recover unobserved outcomes.
column8: Cochrane Handbook chapter 8 · https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-08 · randomization, deviations, measurement and missing outcomes

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Participants who are worsening disproportionately leave a study just before a likely event. Which assumption behind its ordinary Kaplan–Meier estimate is threatened?
column7: Censored participants may have systematically different subsequent event risk from those remaining under observation.
column8: NCI Genomic Data Commons · https://gdc.cancer.gov/content/how-survival-analysis-calculated · Kaplan–Meier survival calculation and censoring
column11: exam::USMLE_Step_3 section::Foundations_of_Independent_Practice topic::Following_an_event-free_cohort source::original outline::stats::interpret outline::stats::population practice::application

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A program reports better five-year survival after screening. Which population endpoint is less vulnerable to lead-time bias when evaluating prevention of death from the target cancer?
column6: Target-cancer mortality in comparable groups from a common start such as randomization.
column7: Keep follow-up comparable. Starting the clock at diagnosis can favor screening without prolonging life.
column8: NCI Cancer Screening Overview PDQ · https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/screening/hp-screening-overview-pdq · lead time, length bias and screening harms

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A periodic screen preferentially identifies slow-growing tumors with long detectable preclinical phases. What explains their better average prognosis compared with symptom-detected tumors?
column7: Slowly progressing lesions have more opportunities to be found at scheduled visits.
column8: NCI Cancer Screening Overview PDQ · https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/screening/hp-screening-overview-pdq · lead time, length bias and screening harms

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Two hospitals each report one maternal death this year, but one has ten times as many live births. Why are raw counts inadequate for comparing maternal mortality?
column6: Different birth denominators imply different maternal mortality ratios.
column7: Small counts also produce imprecise estimates. Case mix and referral patterns matter.
column8: WHO · https://www.who.int/data/gho/indicator-metadata-registry/imr-details/26 · maternal mortality ratio

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Cases and controls are individually matched on age and clinic. Does matching automatically control all confounding in the final estimate?
column6: No. Account for the matching in analysis and consider remaining confounders.
column7: A matched design does not balance unmeasured factors or remove the need for appropriate analysis.
column8: CDC Field Epidemiology Manual · https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/design-conduct-analyze-field-studies.html · sampling, study design and controls

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A budget office needs the total cost predicted for 1,000 similar admissions. Costs have a long right tail. Which location measure multiplied by 1,000 estimates the expected total?
column7: The median can better describe a typical admission but usually cannot be multiplied by the count to estimate total expenditure.
column8: Penn State STAT 200 · https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat200/Lesson02 · distributions, location and variation

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A clinic must tell patients what the middle patient's out-of-pocket bill was. A few extraordinary bills pull the average up. Which measure directly answers the stated question?
column7: Half of observed bills are at or below the median and half at or above. Also explain variability when counseling.
column8: Penn State STAT 200 · https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat200/Lesson02 · distributions, location and variation

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: What distinguishes stopping for futility from stopping for harm?
column6: Futility concerns a low prospect of meeting the trial objective. Harm concerns an unacceptable safety risk.
column7: An independent committee weighs the total evidence under its charter.
column8: FDA, Clinical Trial Data Monitoring Committees · https://www.fda.gov/media/75398/download · interim review, committee independence and recommendations

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A linear model has an exercise coefficient of −2 mm Hg per weekly session with age held constant and no interaction term. What difference does it predict for three versus one weekly session at the same age?
column6: 4 mm Hg lower for three weekly sessions.
column7: Two additional sessions times −2 mm Hg equals −4 mm Hg. A fitted association alone does not establish the effect of prescribing exercise.
column8: Penn State STAT 501 · https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat501/ · multiple linear regression and conditional coefficients

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: After adjusting for age in a linear model, an exposure coefficient is smaller. Does adjustment alone prove the remaining association is causal?
column6: No. Residual confounding, measurement error and model misspecification can remain.
column7: Interpret adjusted estimates in light of design, measurement and causal assumptions.
column8: Penn State STAT 501 · https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat501/ · multiple linear regression and conditional coefficients

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: In a screening cohort, 98 of every 100 negative results are true negatives. What does this say about an individual negative result if the patient is clinically comparable to that cohort?
column6: The estimated probability of still having the condition is about 2%.
column7: This is the complement of NPV. A substantially different pretest risk changes the interpretation.
column8: AHRQ, Test Performance Metrics · https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK98249/ · predictive values, likelihood ratios and ROC curves

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A sponsor widens its noninferiority margin after seeing the primary results. What does this do to the confirmatory claim?
column6: It undermines the prespecified test of acceptable loss.
column7: The margin needs clinical and statistical justification before looking at outcomes.
column8: FDA, Non-Inferiority Clinical Trials · https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/non-inferiority-clinical-trials · choosing the margin and interpreting the confidence interval

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: The confidence interval for a treatment's risk difference crosses zero. Why is a single finite interval entirely on the benefit side inappropriate for its NNT?
column6: At zero difference the reciprocal is unbounded, and a change of sign allows harm.
column7: Report the risk difference and its interval clearly. A finite point NNT can obscure uncertainty about the direction of effect.
column8: Cochrane Handbook chapter 15 · https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-15 · absolute effects, applicability and implications for practice

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A report ranks clinics by the mean of numeric codes assigned arbitrarily to discharge destinations. What should be compared instead?
column6: The proportions discharged to each destination.
column7: Nominal labels cannot be averaged into a meaningful severity score without a separately justified scale.
column8: Penn State STAT 200 · https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat200/Lesson02 · distributions, location and variation

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A lab uses mean ± 1.96 SD as a central 95% reference interval for a strongly right-skewed analyte with a long tail. What assumption should be challenged?
column6: Approximate normality of the individual measurements.
column7: Use an appropriate reference-population method, such as empirical percentiles when sufficiently supported.
column8: NIST Engineering Statistics Handbook · https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/eda/section3/eda3661.htm · normal distribution

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: An observational report gives an odds ratio of 2 for a common outcome. Can the clinician tell the patient that the risk necessarily doubled?
column6: No. An odds ratio of 2 does not generally equal a risk ratio of 2.
column7: With a baseline risk of 0.50, doubling the odds from 1 to 2 gives risk 2/3, a risk ratio of about 1.33.
column8: CDC Field Epidemiology Manual · https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/analyze-interpret-data.html · risk, rates and interpreting comparisons

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A clinician proposes an already approved drug for an indication absent from its FDA label. What does off-label use tell the patient about FDA review?
column6: FDA approval of the product does not establish safety and effectiveness for that particular use.
column7: Discuss the evidence for the proposed use, harms, alternatives and uncertainty.
column8: FDA, Understanding Unapproved Use of Approved Drugs · https://www.fda.gov/understanding-unapproved-use-approved-drugs-label · clinical use outside labeling

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A paper compares left- and right-eye outcomes in the same patients but uses an independent-samples t-test. What dependence has it ignored?
column6: The two observations are paired within each patient.
column7: Analyze within-patient differences or use a suitable correlated-data model. Independent groups would require a different analysis.
column8: NIST Engineering Statistics Handbook · https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/ · tests for two means, contingency tables and confidence intervals

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Two causal exposures have the same individual relative risk and the same unexposed baseline risk. Which produces the larger population attributable fraction, assuming no other differences?
column7: A larger share of the population experiences its excess risk.
column8: CDC, Principles of Epidemiology · https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/csels/dsepd/ss1978/lesson3/ · measures of frequency, association and public health impact

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: An approved drug is studied for uncommon adverse outcomes during routine use after marketing. Which development phase commonly encompasses such studies?
column7: Postmarketing studies can address longer-term safety or effectiveness.
column8: FDA, Step 3 Clinical Research · https://www.fda.gov/patients/drug-development-process/step-3-clinical-research · phases of drug development

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Pain improves in an uncontrolled open-label study. What comparison best separates the specific drug effect from expectations and natural fluctuation when a placebo is ethical?
column6: A randomized, blinded placebo-controlled comparison providing appropriate background care.
column7: A within-group change alone cannot attribute improvement to the drug.
column8: WMA Declaration of Helsinki · https://www.wma.net/policies-post/wma-declaration-of-helsinki/ · risk, consent and use of placebo

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A city is choosing between smoke-free indoor workplaces and offering early lung disease detection. Which is a primary prevention policy targeting a shared exposure?
column7: Reducing exposure before disease develops is primary prevention. Early detection is secondary prevention.
column8: CDC, Principles of Epidemiology · https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/csels/dsepd/ss1978/lesson3/ · measures of frequency, association and public health impact

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Two high-precision trials estimate benefit and harm, respectively, in clinically different populations. What should be assessed before using their pooled mean for a patient?
column6: Whether the differences in population or intervention explain clinically important heterogeneity.
column7: A narrow pooled interval can still conceal important differences in treatment effect.
column8: Cochrane Handbook chapter 10 · https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-10 · forest plots, synthesis and heterogeneity

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Two trials measure pain on different numeric scales that assess the same construct. What kind of continuous effect measure can put them on a common scale for synthesis?
column7: Check direction and comparability of constructs and SDs. The standardization denominator is a within-study measure of spread.
column8: Cochrane Handbook chapter 10 · https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-10 · forest plots, synthesis and heterogeneity

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A primary endpoint is negative. After testing 40 unplanned subgroups, the authors highlight one p-value of 0.03. How should this finding be used?
column6: As hypothesis-generating evidence requiring independent confirmation.
column7: Multiple unplanned looks increase the chance of a favorable result. A subgroup-specific p-value is not a test of interaction.
column8: ICH E9 · https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/E9_Guideline.pdf · sections 3 and 5, trial size, estimation, multiplicity and subgroups

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A tightly controlled trial provides free medication, daily coaching and perfect follow-up. A clinic with routine adherence expects a smaller benefit. Which distinction is relevant?
column6: Efficacy under controlled conditions versus effectiveness in routine care.
column7: Delivery, adherence and access can change realized benefit.
column8: Penn State STAT 507 · https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat507/Lesson08 · confounding, bias, random error and effect modification

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: An informed patient understands the expected benefit of treatment but places a high value on avoiding daily treatment burden. What information belongs in the decision alongside the event risks?
column6: The patient's preferences about benefits, harms and treatment burden.
column7: Explore the tradeoff and agree on a plan consistent with the informed patient's values.
column8: Cochrane Handbook chapter 15 · https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-15 · absolute effects, applicability and implications for practice

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Researchers choose a primary outcome and analysis after looking through many endpoints. What prospective practice makes the next study's test confirmatory?
column6: Specify the hypothesis, endpoints and analysis plan before examining outcomes.
column7: This distinguishes a planned test from exploratory selection driven by the data.
column8: ICH E9 · https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/E9_Guideline.pdf · sections 3 and 5, trial size, estimation, multiplicity and subgroups

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A team obtains a Common Rule consent waiver for an identifiable chart review at a HIPAA-covered institution. Does that alone document permission for the HIPAA research disclosure?
column6: No. Establish an applicable HIPAA authorization or permitted disclosure pathway, such as a properly documented HIPAA waiver.
column7: Human-subject consent and authorization for use of protected health information have distinct requirements.
column8: HHS, HIPAA and Research · https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/special-topics/research/index.html · authorization, IRB or Privacy Board waivers

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Two tests both measure the same biological marker. Can their false-positive probabilities automatically be multiplied to calculate the chance that both are positive in someone without disease?
column6: No. Use the conditional probability for the second result given the first, unless conditional independence is justified.
column7: Shared measurement errors can make joint false positives more common than an independence calculation predicts.
column8: OpenStax, Introductory Statistics 2e · https://openstax.org/books/introductory-statistics-2e/pages/3-3-two-basic-rules-of-probability · joint, conditional and union probabilities

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Path A gives four years at utility 0.50. Path B gives three years at utility 0.80. Ignoring discounting, which yields more QALYs and by how much?
column7: B gives 2.4 versus 2.0 for A. An individual patient's preferences may differ from the utility estimates.
column8: NICE, health technology evaluations manual · https://www.nice.org.uk/process/pmg36/ · reference case and health effects in QALYs

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A purposive interview sample contains 12 participants. Nine mention cost. Can 75% be reported as the prevalence of this barrier in the whole patient population?
column6: No. Purposive sampling supports understanding experiences, not a population prevalence estimate.
column7: A representative sample and suitable measurement are needed for prevalence estimation.
column8: CDC Field Epidemiology Manual · https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/qualitative-data.html · qualitative inquiry and purposive sampling

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A patient asks whether 12 events per 100 person-years means exactly 12 of every 100 people will have an event in one year. What distinction matters?
column6: An incidence rate uses person-time, while a one-year risk is a probability among people initially at risk.
column7: A rate cannot simply be read as an exact cumulative probability.
column8: CDC, Principles of Epidemiology · https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/csels/dsepd/ss1978/lesson3/ · measures of frequency, association and public health impact

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A town needs the number of residents likely to need ongoing diabetes services now. Should it multiply the resident count by current prevalence or by last year's incidence rate?
column6: Use the current prevalence in the same population.
column7: Prevalence describes existing cases, including long-term survivors. An incidence rate describes newly occurring events per person-time.
column8: CDC, Principles of Epidemiology · https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/csels/dsepd/ss1978/lesson3/ · measures of frequency, association and public health impact

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A patient asks what a study can tell them about survival. Which endpoint is directly relevant to a claim about living longer?
column6: A survival or mortality endpoint measured over appropriate follow-up.
column7: Improvement in a symptom, biomarker or composite alone does not establish a mortality benefit.
column8: Cochrane Handbook chapter 15 · https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-15 · absolute effects, applicability and implications for practice

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A case-control study relies on remote exposure recall. Which alternative measurement could reduce differential recall?
column6: A consistently recorded exposure measure collected before disease onset.
column7: Check that record completeness and exposure definitions are comparable in cases and controls.
column8: Penn State STAT 507 · https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat507/Lesson08 · confounding, bias, random error and effect modification

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A clinic enrolls patients only on their worst symptom day, treats all of them and finds lower scores a week later. What design feature could distinguish a treatment effect from regression toward the mean?
column6: A concurrent comparable control group selected by the same extreme baseline criterion, ideally randomized.
column7: Both groups would experience the selection effect. A before-after change alone cannot isolate the treatment effect.
column8: AHRQ Methods Guide · https://effectivehealthcare.ahrq.gov/sites/default/files/pdf/single-group-studies_white-paper.pdf · interpreting changes in single-arm studies

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A well-randomized trial has extensive missing outcomes and unmasked subjective outcome ratings. Can a high total quality score settle whether its effect estimate is trustworthy?
column6: No. Evaluate bias in the relevant domains for that specific result.
column7: Strength in randomization cannot cancel bias from measurement or missing outcomes.
column8: Cochrane Handbook chapter 8 · https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-08 · randomization, deviations, measurement and missing outcomes

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A strong risk model includes a fixed patient characteristic. A colleague interprets its large coefficient as the expected benefit of changing that characteristic. What inference is unsupported?
column6: A predictive association alone cannot identify the effect of an intervention.
column7: An intervention effect needs a well-defined comparison and credible causal assumptions.
column8: CDC, Principles of Epidemiology · https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/csels/dsepd/ss1978/lesson3/ · measures of frequency, association and public health impact

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A patient values avoiding a disabling stroke much more than avoiding a transient rash. Can the NNT for stroke and NNH for rash alone determine the right choice?
column6: No. Discuss the probabilities together with the severity and value of each outcome to the patient.
column7: Event counts alone treat unlike outcomes as if they had equal consequences.
column8: Cochrane Handbook chapter 15 · https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-15 · absolute effects, applicability and implications for practice

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A team wants to read positive predictive value directly off a receiver operating characteristic curve. What additional population quantity is needed?
column6: The pretest probability or prevalence in the target population.
column7: Sensitivity and false-positive rate condition on disease status. Predictive value conditions on test result.
column8: AHRQ, Test Performance Metrics · https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK98249/ · predictive values, likelihood ratios and ROC curves

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Before starting a U.S. study, an investigator asks whether IRB approval alone settles the requirements for handling a federally controlled study drug. What must also be checked?
column6: Applicable controlled-substance registration and handling requirements for that drug and activity.
column7: IRB approval addresses human-subject protections. DEA requirements depend on the controlled substance and research activity.
column8: DEA Diversion Control Division, Researcher’s Manual · https://www.deadiversion.usdoj.gov/pubs/manuals/manuals.html · registration and controlled-substance requirements

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: An investigator changes the trial's dose schedule to improve convenience, with no immediate hazard requiring a change. What should happen before using the amendment in an IRB-reviewed study?
column6: Submit the proposed change for required approval before implementation.
column7: Changes needed immediately to eliminate an apparent hazard have a specific exception. Document and report according to requirements.
column8: HHS, Protection of Human Subjects · https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-A/part-46/subpart-A · §§46.108, 46.111, 46.116, review, risk and consent

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: An accurate blood test detects an asymptomatic condition earlier, but early treatment confers no demonstrated health benefit and false positives prompt invasive procedures. Is accuracy alone sufficient to recommend population screening?
column6: No. Evaluate patient-important benefits and harms of the entire screening pathway.
column7: Consider overdiagnosis, downstream testing, treatment effectiveness and the population offered screening.
column8: NCI Cancer Screening Overview PDQ · https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/screening/hp-screening-overview-pdq · lead time, length bias and screening harms

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A treatment trial excludes participants with advanced kidney disease. What problem arises when applying its result to a patient receiving dialysis?
column6: The effect and harms may differ in a group excluded from the trial.
column7: Check eligibility and evidence from clinically comparable patients.
column8: CDC Field Epidemiology Manual · https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/analyze-interpret-data.html · risk, rates and interpreting comparisons
column11: exam::USMLE_Step_3 section::Foundations_of_Independent_Practice topic::Identifying_sampling_and_allocation_from_a_study_description source::original outline::stats::decide outline::stats::design outline::stats::interpret practice::application

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A small community has too few deaths for stable age-specific local rates. Reliable external rates and local age counts are available. How can an expected count be constructed?
column6: Multiply each external age-specific rate by the corresponding local population or person-time and sum.
column7: Match rate units to denominators. This is the basis for indirect standardization.
column8: Penn State STAT 507 · https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat507/Lesson03 · disease occurrence and standardization

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A report labels tiny standard-error bars around the group mean as the range of individual patient responses. What should represent variation among patients?
column6: A distributional summary such as SD, an interquartile range or individual observations.
column7: A standard error measures uncertainty in the estimated mean. It can shrink even when individual responses remain widely dispersed.
column8: Penn State STAT 200 · https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat200/Lesson02 · distributions, location and variation

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: From the SPRINT figure alone, can the size of the effect on stroke as an individual endpoint be determined?
column6: No. The bars summarize a composite outcome.
column7: A component-specific conclusion requires the stroke data and their uncertainty.
column8: SPRINT Research Group, original trial report · https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1511939 · study population, primary endpoint and incidence rates. Figure redrawn from published aggregate data.
column11: exam::USMLE_Step_3 section::Foundations_of_Independent_Practice topic::Reading_published_prevention_trials source::original visual::question outline::stats::decide outline::stats::interpret practice::transfer

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A patient with diabetes asks whether the original SPRINT result directly estimates their personal benefit. What enrollment feature limits direct application?
column7: The trial studied adults at elevated cardiovascular risk. Assess other applicable evidence and the patient's risks and preferences.
column8: SPRINT Research Group, original trial report · https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1511939 · study population, primary endpoint and incidence rates. Figure redrawn from published aggregate data.

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A retirement community has a higher crude death rate than a neighboring town but equal age-specific death rates in every age stratum. What accounts for the crude difference?
column7: Directly standardizing both communities to the same age weights gives identical adjusted rates.
column8: Penn State STAT 507 · https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat507/Lesson03 · disease occurrence and standardization

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A prespecified interim analysis finds the probability of reaching the efficacy objective is very low if enrollment continues. What type of stopping recommendation might be considered?
column7: Futility is distinct from demonstrated harm or demonstrated equivalence.
column8: FDA, Clinical Trial Data Monitoring Committees · https://www.fda.gov/media/75398/download · interim review, committee independence and recommendations

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: An independent monitoring committee sees an unexpected serious harm imbalance. Must it wait for a planned efficacy boundary to be crossed before considering a safety recommendation?
column6: No. Assess the harm signal promptly under the charter and advise on participant protection.
column7: The efficacy stopping rule serves a different purpose from ongoing safety assessment.
column8: FDA, Clinical Trial Data Monitoring Committees · https://www.fda.gov/media/75398/download · interim review, committee independence and recommendations

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A small trial recruits at three hospitals with very different baseline risk. How can randomization be designed to promote treatment balance within each hospital?
column6: Randomize within strata defined by hospital.
column7: This preserves chance allocation within each hospital and reduces the chance of large site imbalance.
column8: Cochrane Handbook chapter 8 · https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-08 · randomization, deviations, measurement and missing outcomes

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A new electronic reporting system doubles the number of clinics submitting cases. Notifications rise abruptly while standardized sentinel rates stay flat. What should be checked first?
column6: The change in reporting coverage and completeness.
column7: Ascertainment can raise reported counts without a corresponding increase in disease incidence.
column8: CDC, Updated Guidelines for Evaluating Public Health Surveillance Systems · https://stacks.cdc.gov/view/cdc/248461 · purpose, completeness and timeliness of reporting

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A hospital wants a community prevalence estimate but recruited exclusively through its specialty clinic. What sampling change would better address the stated target?

column8: IHS · https://ichd-3.org/ · NICE · https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg150/chapter/Recommendations · US prescribing information · https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=1909558d-8342-4af0-9487-eecdaac70070 · Oxygen crossover trial · https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19996400/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: In a series of 133 spontaneous spinal cord infarctions, 102 patients reached severe deficits within 12 hours. Approximately what fraction did so?
column7: Divide 102 by 133. The remainder illustrates why a less abrupt course cannot exclude infarction.
column8: Zalewski et al. · https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6440254/ · Serial imaging study · https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23091532/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: In a published series of diagnosed spinal infarction cases, 30 patients with available initial imaging had a normal initial spinal MRI (24%). Why is 24% not the probability of infarction after a normal MRI in a new patient?
column6: The denominator consists of people with infarction, not everyone presenting with a normal MRI.
column7: The reverse probability also depends on how often new patients without infarction have that result.
column8: Zalewski et al. · https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6440254/ · Serial imaging study · https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23091532/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: In Nordsten-DS a responder had a reduction of at least 30% from baseline on the Oswestry Disability Index. A participant falls from 50 to 37 points. Does this meet the responder criterion?
column7: Use change relative to the baseline score.
column8: Nordsten-DS · https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2024-079771

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Nordsten-DS enrolled surgical candidates with symptomatic lumbar stenosis and degenerative spondylolisthesis. Can it determine whether a patient with an unstable traumatic fracture needs instrumentation?
column6: No. The fracture and instability involve a different indication.
column7: The trial estimates outcomes for its studied clinical population.
column8: Nordsten-DS · https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2024-079771

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Does the interval in this figure cross the prespecified inferiority boundary for decompression alone?
column6: No. Its lower limit is above the −15 percentage point boundary.
column7: The endpoint is a clinically meaningful reduction in disability, so a negative difference favors fusion.
column8: Nordsten-DS · https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2024-079771

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: At five years the estimated responder difference for decompression alone minus fusion was +0.4 percentage points, with a 95% interval of −11.2 to +11.9. Does this demonstrate superiority?
column6: No. The interval includes zero and effects in either direction.
column7: Meeting a prespecified noninferiority margin answers a different question.
column8: Nordsten-DS · https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2024-079771

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: What gestational-age condition defined the TABLET primary live-birth endpoint?
column6: Live birth at or beyond 34 completed weeks.
column7: The trial enrolled euthyroid TPO-antibody-positive women trying to conceive.
column8: Dhillon-Smith et al. · TABLET trial, Table 5 · https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK547631/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: The trial table lists 176 qualifying births among 470 participants with primary outcome data in the levothyroxine arm. About what percentage met the primary endpoint?
column7: Divide 176 by 470. The denominator includes participants who did not become pregnant.
column8: Dhillon-Smith et al. · TABLET trial, Table 5 · https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK547631/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A TABLET participant delivered a live infant at 32 weeks. How would this birth count for the prespecified primary endpoint?
column6: It would not count as a live birth at or beyond 34 weeks.
column7: It would count in an outcome that included earlier live births.
column8: Dhillon-Smith et al. · TABLET trial, Table 5 · https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK547631/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Which thyroid function state did TABLET require at enrollment despite positive TPO antibodies?
column7: The trial investigated adding levothyroxine before conception to patients with normal thyroid function.
column8: Dhillon-Smith et al. · TABLET trial, Table 5 · https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK547631/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: In TABLET the relative risk was 0.97 with 95% CI 0.83–1.14. What does that interval establish about superiority for the primary live-birth outcome?
column7: The interval spans 1 and allows effects in either direction. It does not establish exact equivalence.
column8: Dhillon-Smith et al. · TABLET trial, Table 5 · https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK547631/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A patient trying to conceive has persistent TSH 31 mIU/L and low free T4. Why would the TABLET result be a poor reason to withhold levothyroxine?
column6: Overt hypothyroidism was outside the trial population.
column7: This patient has a replacement indication that euthyroid trial participants did not.
column8: Dhillon-Smith et al. · TABLET trial, Table 5 · https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK547631/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: For a risk difference between varenicline and placebo, which value represents equal risk?
column7: Subtracting equal risks gives zero.
column8: Anthenelli et al. · EAGLES · https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27116918/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: In the EAGLES psychiatric cohort, the 95% interval for varenicline minus placebo on the primary neuropsychiatric endpoint was −0.42 to +3.59 percentage points. Does this exclude an increase?
column6: No. The interval includes both zero and positive risk differences.
column7: The trial concerned clinically stable participants. Absence of a statistically significant increase does not establish identical risk.
column8: Anthenelli et al. · EAGLES · https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27116918/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: For the EAGLES nonpsychiatric cohort the corresponding interval was −2.40 to −0.15 percentage points. Which direction is supported for this endpoint in this cohort?
column6: Lower risk with varenicline than placebo for this comparison.
column7: Both limits are below zero. Direct comparison of the two subgroup intervals alone is not an interaction test.
column8: Anthenelli et al. · EAGLES · https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27116918/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: What primary outcome did the randomized ED-initiated buprenorphine trial assess at 30 days?
column7: This endpoint measures treatment engagement. It does not directly measure abstinence or mortality.
column8: D’Onofrio et al. · https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25919527/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: From the displayed trial data, what was the approximate absolute difference in 30-day engagement between the ED buprenorphine strategy and referral alone?
column6: 41 percentage points higher with the buprenorphine strategy.
column7: Subtract about 37% from 78%. The strategy also included linkage to follow-up.
column8: D’Onofrio et al. · https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25919527/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: In the ED trial, engagement was 78% with the buprenorphine strategy and 45% with brief intervention plus referral. What is the absolute difference for this comparison?
column7: Changing the comparator changes the estimated contrast even though the intervention outcome stays fixed.
column8: D’Onofrio et al. · https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25919527/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: The figure shows six-week survival in the upper GI bleeding trial. What was the absolute survival advantage for the restrictive group?
column7: The estimated survival probabilities were 95% and 91%.
column8: Transfusion Strategies for Acute Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding · https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1211801

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: In a randomized trial of severe upper GI bleeding, what do assigned thresholds of 7 and 9 g/dL specify?
column6: The hemoglobin levels below which transfusion was triggered in each strategy.
column7: They are intervention thresholds, not post-transfusion targets.
column8: Transfusion Strategies for Acute Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding · https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1211801

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A patient with upper GI bleeding is exsanguinating before hemoglobin has equilibrated. Does this trial support waiting for a value below 7 g/dL before emergency transfusion?
column6: No. Patients needing immediate transfusion for massive exsanguinating bleeding were excluded.
column7: The trial does not establish a delay threshold for this emergency.
column8: Transfusion Strategies for Acute Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding · https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1211801

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Older patients are more likely to receive a drug and more likely to fall even without it. Which measured variable should be considered in estimating the drug's total effect on falls?
column7: It is a pre-exposure common cause in the stated comparison.
column8: Hernán and Robins · Causal Inference: What If · https://miguelhernan.org/s/hernanrobins_WhatIf_2jan25.pdf

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: What is a collider on a causal path?
column6: A variable into which two arrows on that path point.
column7: Conditioning on a common effect can open a previously blocked path.
column8: Hernán and Robins · Causal Inference: What If · https://miguelhernan.org/s/hernanrobins_WhatIf_2jan25.pdf

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Treatment and underlying severity both cause extra clinic visits. Analysts restrict to people who made an extra visit. What pathway can this create between treatment and severity?
column6: A spurious association from conditioning on their common effect, the extra visit.
column7: Opening this path can bias the treatment–outcome comparison.
column8: Hernán and Robins · Causal Inference: What If · https://miguelhernan.org/s/hernanrobins_WhatIf_2jan25.pdf

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: In a study using dispenser activations per dispenser-hour, what additional denominator is needed to estimate adherence to indicated hand hygiene?
column6: The number of eligible hand hygiene opportunities, linked to corresponding actions.
column7: Dispenses per hour can also change with patient traffic or repeated use.
column8: Srigley et al. · Observation and hand hygiene monitoring · https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25002555/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Electronic dispenser activity is about threefold higher in hallways within sight of auditors. May the ward report that a specified percentage of all indicated opportunities received hand hygiene from these data alone?
column6: No. The activity rate lacks the eligible-opportunity denominator.
column7: The published comparison supports a concern about observation effects but does not itself measure the fraction of opportunities fulfilled.
column8: Srigley et al. · Observation and hand hygiene monitoring · https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25002555/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Using the trial record, could the true event risk among the intervention participants exceed the complete control risk?
column6: Yes. It could reach 14%, above 10% in controls.
column7: Six confirmed events plus eight missing among 100 permit risks from 6% to 14%.
column8: Cochrane Handbook · Assessing risk of bias in a randomized trial · https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-08 · Original teaching figure

column4: For a binary event, how do you compute the largest possible risk when final outcomes are missing?

column4: In this other record, could any assignment of the missing intervention outcomes produce an event risk as high as control?

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: What timing information is absent when exposure and prevalent disease are measured only once at the same visit?
column6: Whether the exposure preceded the disease process.

column8: CDC · Field Epidemiology Manual · Analyzing and interpreting data · https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/analyze-interpret-data.html

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A cohort measures diet one month before diagnosis, but patients report changing their diet because of months of prodromal symptoms. What threat survives the prospective recording date?
column6: Reverse causation from the prodromal illness.
column7: A prediagnosis date alone does not establish that diet preceded disease onset.
column8: CDC · Field Epidemiology Manual · Analyzing and interpreting data · https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/analyze-interpret-data.html

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: What is the null hypothesis for a Pearson chi-square test of independence?
column6: The two categorical variables are independent in the population.
column7: A small p-value flags incompatibility with independence under the test assumptions.
column8: OpenStax · Introductory Statistics 2e · Test of independence · https://openstax.org/books/introductory-statistics-2e/pages/11-3-test-of-independence

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Discharge destination has three categories and differs by treatment on an omnibus chi-square test. Can the committee conclude that home discharge specifically increased?
column6: No. Inspect the home-discharge risks or a prespecified contrast with uncertainty.
column7: The omnibus result could arise from redistribution between the other categories.
column8: OpenStax · Introductory Statistics 2e · Test of independence · https://openstax.org/books/introductory-statistics-2e/pages/11-3-test-of-independence

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A committee treats a nonsignificant 8-week risk difference as proof of interchangeability. Its 90% interval is −9 to +7 points and its equivalence margins are ±3. Does this support interchangeability?
column6: No. The interval extends beyond both margins.
column7: Failing to reject a zero difference can coexist with substantial uncertainty.
column8: ICH · E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials · https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/E9_Guideline.pdf

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: What must be specified about acceptable differences before an equivalence comparison is interpreted?
column6: The lower and upper equivalence margins.
column7: The corresponding interval must fit within both limits to rule out differences considered too large.
column8: ICH · E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials · https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/E9_Guideline.pdf

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: When a study improves a surrogate, what additional evidence is needed to claim a particular patient outcome improved?
column6: Evidence connecting the intervention effect to that clinical outcome in the relevant context.
column7: The strongest direct evidence measures the clinical outcome in a suitable comparative study.
column8: CAST Investigators · Arrhythmia suppression after myocardial infarction (preliminary report) · https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2473403/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: The CAST record reports arrhythmic death or nonfatal cardiac arrest. Which group had the higher observed event proportion?
column6: The encainide or flecainide group, about 4.5% versus 1.2% with placebo.
column7: The proportions use randomized participants as the denominators. Marker suppression alone had suggested a different clinical expectation.
column8: CAST Investigators · Arrhythmia suppression after myocardial infarction (preliminary report) · https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2473403/

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: What feature of repeated measurements on one patient invalidates treating them as separate independent patients?
column7: Ignoring it can give the wrong standard error and degrees of freedom.
column8: OpenStax · Introductory Statistics 2e · Matched or paired samples · https://openstax.org/books/introductory-statistics-2e/pages/10-4-matched-or-paired-samples

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A lab compares two independent patient groups. Each patient contributes three aliquots from one blood draw. What should supply the independent sample sizes for a comparison of patient means?
column6: The patients in the two groups.
column7: Analyze patient summaries or model the within-patient replicates. Aliquots alone do not increase the patient count.
column8: OpenStax · Introductory Statistics 2e · Matched or paired samples · https://openstax.org/books/introductory-statistics-2e/pages/10-4-matched-or-paired-samples

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Clinicians titrate analgesic dose upward for patients with the most persistent pain. High-dose users subsequently report more pain. Does the association establish that escalating the dose caused worse pain?
column6: No. Baseline pain severity influenced dose selection.
column7: Evaluate pre-exposure prognosis and the treatment assignment process.
column8: Hernán and Robins · Causal Inference: What If · https://miguelhernan.org/s/hernanrobins_WhatIf_2jan25.pdf

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Why can a worse outcome at higher prescribed doses occur even if the treatment itself helps?
column6: Sicker patients may be given higher doses and have worse baseline prognosis.
column7: This is confounding by indication.
column8: Hernán and Robins · Causal Inference: What If · https://miguelhernan.org/s/hernanrobins_WhatIf_2jan25.pdf

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A trial randomly assigns several doses before treatment, preserves follow-up and finds larger symptom improvements with higher assigned doses. Which feature most strengthens the causal interpretation compared with clinician-selected doses?
column6: Randomization of dose breaks its systematic link to baseline prognosis in expectation.
column7: Adherence, precision and outcome ascertainment still require review.
column8: Hernán and Robins · Causal Inference: What If · https://miguelhernan.org/s/hernanrobins_WhatIf_2jan25.pdf

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Before using an ecological finding, what feature of the intended decision should be specified?
column6: Whether the target is an individual outcome or a group-level burden.
column7: The evidence needs to address that level of inference.
column8: CDC · Field Epidemiology Manual · Analyzing and interpreting data · https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/analyze-interpret-data.html

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A county wants to place a mobile clinic in the neighborhood with the largest total number of untreated cases. Can accurate neighborhood case counts address that placement criterion?
column6: Yes. Total neighborhood burden is itself the target.
column7: No inference about which particular resident has the condition is needed to rank the neighborhoods.
column8: CDC · Field Epidemiology Manual · Analyzing and interpreting data · https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/analyze-interpret-data.html

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: For a service offered in routine practice, which patients should contribute to an estimate of the effect of the offer?
column6: All eligible patients assigned to the offer under the study design, including those who do not take it up.
column7: Restricting analysis to adherent users answers a different question and can select on prognosis.
column8: Loudon et al. · PRECIS-2 and trial design · https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.h2147

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A health system randomizes clinics to offer an adherence program using ordinary staffing. All eligible patients are followed whether or not they attend. What effect does the assigned-group comparison estimate?
column6: The effect of offering the program as implemented in those clinics.
column7: Uptake and nonattendance are part of the real-world policy effect.
column8: Loudon et al. · PRECIS-2 and trial design · https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.h2147

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: In a cohort, baseline frailty predicts falls with p<0.001. Does this p-value quantify the probability that treating frailty would prevent a fall?
column6: No. It concerns an association in the fitted model.
column7: An intervention effect needs an appropriate causal comparison.
column8: American Statistical Association · Statement on p-values · https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2016.1154108

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Which hypothesis should a reader identify before interpreting a reported p-value?
column6: The particular null hypothesis and comparison used to calculate it.
column7: It may differ from the comparison a headline claims.
column8: American Statistical Association · Statement on p-values · https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2016.1154108

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Only the intervention arm's before-and-after change is tested and gives p=0.002. What comparison would address efficacy in this parallel randomized trial?
column6: Compare outcomes between the randomized treatment and control groups with an appropriate estimate and uncertainty.
column7: A within-arm change alone can reflect natural history and other common changes.
column8: American Statistical Association · Statement on p-values · https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2016.1154108

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: Which feature makes a reference exposure record useful for investigating recall bias?
column6: It was recorded independently of later case status and measures the relevant exposure.
column7: A reference that omits the exposure cannot resolve the question.
column8: CDC · Field Epidemiology Manual · Analyzing and interpreting data · https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/analyze-interpret-data.html

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: An analyst proposes validating reports of nonprescription aspirin with an insurance database that records only prescription fills. What key limitation remains?
column6: The database misses the over-the-counter exposure being investigated.
column7: A missing claim cannot establish that a participant's recollection was false.
column8: CDC · Field Epidemiology Manual · Analyzing and interpreting data · https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/analyze-interpret-data.html

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: What kinds of evidence help apply a trustworthy trial result to a substantially different target population?
column6: Evidence about relevant effect modifiers, baseline risks, harms and delivery in that population.
column7: Eligibility alone does not establish that the treatment effect will be different or unchanged.
column8: Cochrane Handbook · Assessing risk of bias in a randomized trial · https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-08

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A randomized trial included the target patients, but worsening patients in one arm stopped follow-up. Would recruiting a broader age range resolve the current effect estimate's main weakness?
column6: No. Examine missing outcomes and sensitivity to plausible assumptions.
column7: The current threat concerns validity within the enrolled sample.
column8: Cochrane Handbook · Assessing risk of bias in a randomized trial · https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-08

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: What features should be similar across randomized groups to isolate the specific effect of a treatment component?
column6: The cointerventions and treatment context apart from that component.
column7: Differences in visits, expectations or additional care can contribute to a bundled effect.
column8: Cochrane Handbook · Assessing risk of bias in a randomized trial · https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-08

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A new clinic program combines a procedure, weekly visits and coaching and is randomized against usual care. Patients report better function. Can the committee attribute the whole difference specifically to the procedure?
column6: No. Assignment changed several components together.
column7: The trial estimates the effect of the program as delivered.
column8: Cochrane Handbook · Assessing risk of bias in a randomized trial · https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-08

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: What should support a subgroup-specific treatment claim beyond a convincing biologic rationale?
column6: A directly estimated difference in treatment effects with uncertainty and a credible prespecified analysis.
column7: Consider scale, multiplicity, adequate data and consistency with other evidence.
column8: ICH · E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials · https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/E9_Guideline.pdf

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A prespecified test estimates the difference between subgroup-specific treatment risk differences at 8 points, 95% CI 4 to 12. Which claim is supported on this scale?
column6: The absolute treatment effects differ between these subgroups.
column7: The interval for the difference excludes zero. Appropriate subgroup decisions still require each group's benefits and harms.
column8: ICH · E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials · https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/E9_Guideline.pdf

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: What must be comparable over time before rising notification counts can be interpreted as rising disease occurrence?
column6: The population covered and the process for finding and reporting cases.
column7: An apparent increase can be produced at several points in surveillance.
column8: CDC · Field Epidemiology Manual · Analyzing and interpreting data · https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/analyze-interpret-data.html

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: After a reporting expansion, the same continuously participating clinics also show higher age-specific rates with unchanged testing, case definition and catchment. Does the added number of reporters fully explain this finding?
column6: No. Investigate a rise within the stable surveillance population.
column7: The stable-site analysis removes the mechanical increase from incorporating more clinics.
column8: CDC · Field Epidemiology Manual · Analyzing and interpreting data · https://www.cdc.gov/field-epi-manual/php/chapters/analyze-interpret-data.html

column2: MCAT and USMLE::USMLE Step 3::Foundations of Independent Practice
column4: A trial tests mortality first, then admission, stopping at the first failed test. Mortality gives p=0.14 and admission p=0.002. What status does the admission finding have?
column6: Descriptive or exploratory under this plan.
column7: The first test did not open the gate for confirmatory testing of admissions.
column8: FDA · Multiple Endpoints in Clinical Trials · https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/multiple-endpoints-clinical-trials
